findings.title: Target kernel and baseline are ambiguous after slice 148
findings.description:
- Slice 149 lists only `[145]` as a dependency. Its problem statement is built on "Slice 148's Phase 2 measurements".
- Slice 148 is marked `status: complete`. It adds a tiled kernel with `qd.sync()` cooperative tile loads and renames the backends at ship time. `quadrants-fused` then points at the tiled kernel, and the untiled one becomes `quadrants-fused-untiled`.
- Slice 149 never says which kernel gets the `break` and `S`: the untiled one, the tiled one, or both. 148 says seam changes must apply "symmetrically" to both.
- The design is written against the untiled structure (`for kk in range(start, end)`, `quadrants_fused_kernels.py` line numbers).
- A thread-divergent `break` inside a cooperative tile-load loop that contains `qd.sync()` is a barrier-deadlock hazard. The design doesn't consider it.
- The baseline is "slice 145, 38 TPS". The plan shows 148 targeting 60 TPS, so the design should say whether that baseline is still the starting state.
- Fix: add 148 to the dependencies. Name the kernel(s) modified and the backend name used for gate runs. State the baseline kernel and its TPS. If the tiled kernel is in scope, say how the break interacts with the sync points.

findings.title: `cell_size` and `S` are independent inputs with an unchecked invariant
findings.description:
- The Component Interactions diagram (lines 84-100) has `BenchConfig` hold both `cell_size` (= `query_radius / S`) and `S`, and passes both to the kernel.
- The scan window only covers the query radius when `S * cell_size >= query_radius`.
- If the two drift, neighbors are silently missed. This is a hidden coupling with no failure mode named.
- The validation only checks `S` (lines 71-76).
- Fix: derive `cell_size` from `query_radius` and `S` in one place and don't accept it independently. Or validate the invariant at config load and fail loudly.
- The design should also say where `S` lives for slice 146's production path. The gate default is `S=3` for bench runs only. Slice 146 inherits `S=1` unless the config surface is defined.

findings.title: Subdivision gain math is wrong, and the interaction with early exit is unanalyzed
findings.description:
- The design says S=3 alone drops candidates loaded to "~5000" and that both interventions give "~555".
- With 49 cells of about 555 agents each, S=3 loads about 27k candidates. The scan area ratio is (7/3)²/9 ≈ 0.6, so about a 40% reduction, not 9×.
- Early exit is a `break` on the innermost `kk` loop only. After the cap is hit, the `drow`/`dcol` loops still run all remaining cells. That is 49 iterations at S=3 versus 9 at S=1, each reading cell boundaries.
- With early exit in place, S=3 may give little or no gain and may add overhead. Yet `S=3` is already fixed as the gate configuration (line 128).
- Intervention 2 is assigned to this slice by the plan, so it shouldn't be dropped. The design should still do three things:
  - Correct the arithmetic.
  - Say how the outer loops are guarded (for example, skip the cell scan once the cap is reached).
  - Make the gate configuration follow the ablation results rather than presume `S=3`. If early exit alone clears 100 TPS, `S>1` is added complexity with no measured benefit.

findings.title: The seam claim contradicts the Option A design
findings.description:
- The slice plan entry says early exit replaces counter-gating inside `get_neighbors_first_k`. The design puts the `break` in the caller and keeps the seam as a guard.
- That duplicates the cap condition in two places, which breaks DRY. The seam's own cap check becomes dead logic.
- Line 99 says the seam is "now unreachable after break". That is inaccurate, because it is still called for the first k candidates.
- A distance-ranked k-nearest (A7) must visit all candidates, so the caller's `break` has to be removed at that point. The seam is therefore not a drop-in swap point, and "A7 seam preserved" (line 112) overstates it.
- Fix: state that the cap lives in one place. Say plainly that A7 will have to remove the caller's break.

findings.title: The four-way ablation in the walkthrough is not reproducible
findings.description:
- Step 3 lists four configurations. The "baseline" and "early exit only" commands are identical, and so are "S=3 counter-gating" and "both".
- Early exit is an unconditional replacement (Option A) with no toggle, so counter-gating cannot be selected at runtime.
- Without a toggle or a pinned reference backend, the ablation can't be run. That undermines the attribution A2 and A3 depend on, and the decision about whether `S>1` is worth keeping.
- Fix: either specify the reference (for example, the pre-change backend or commit used for baseline numbers) or cut the ablation down to what can be measured.

findings.title: Warp-divergence argument and parity risk at S>1
findings.description:
- The claim that threads in a warp have similar spatial index and hit the cap at similar iterations assumes agents are dispatched in spatial order. The design doesn't state the dispatch order.
- Selection is first-k in scan order. At S=1 the first-k set is unchanged by the break. At S=3 the scan order changes, so the set of accepted neighbors changes. That is an anisotropic bias toward the first rows scanned.
- A4 (within 20% of numpy) is the right gate, but the design should acknowledge the risk.

findings.title: `S` upper bound is an inline magic constant with an unsupported rationale
findings.description:
- The `8` is hard-coded in the validation snippet. Project rules call for centralizing constants at config level.
- The memory justification isn't supported. Grid dimensions grow by S² against a world of a few thousand cells. The kernel's scan size is not an auxiliary array.
- Either define the cap once in config with a real reason, or drop it.

findings.title: NFR restated, scope matches the plan entry, and no new I/O paths
findings.description:
- The Tier 2 NFR (60 TPS at N=50k on CUDA) is restated with the specific A3 gate of at least 100 TPS and its headroom rationale.
- Exit criteria (≥5× `force_total`, ≥100 TPS, 20% parity) match the plan's entry for slice 149.
- No external API changes are made. The slice adds no I/O or message paths, so there are no new failure modes to enumerate.
